original_target.title: Can a nonresonant elliptic equilibrium be unstable in an analytic two-degree Hamiltonian?

scope_comparison: The September density theorem requires d>=5 and Fayad's analytic instability examples start in d=3. A divergent Birkhoff normal form in d=2 is not an escaping trajectory; Gevrey examples have weaker regularity. The new Zenodo announcement is conditional finite-time Nekhoroshev confinement, not all-time Lyapunov stability or an unstable analytic two-degree example.
